name: HashiCorp Consul
description: Self-hosted HashiCorp Consul reads: the agent's own configuration, the services registered in the catalogue, the nodes in the catalogue, the health instances of one service, and one KV entry by key. Read-only; every register, deregister, KV write, session, ACL and maintenance-mode endpoint on the same API is deliberately absent.

tools.name: agent_self
tools.description: Get the configuration and cluster identity of the Consul agent this credential points at: datacenter, node name, version and whether it is a server

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List the service names registered in the Consul catalogue, each with its tags

dc.description: Optional datacenter to query instead of the agent's own

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description: List the nodes registered in the Consul catalogue, with their addresses and datacenter

dc.description: Optional datacenter to query instead of the agent's own

filter.description: Optional Consul filter expression, e.g. Meta.rack == r1

tools.name: health_service
tools.description: List the instances of one service with their node, port, tags and health checks, optionally only the passing ones

service.description: Registered service name, as returned by list_services

dc.description: Optional datacenter to query instead of the agent's own

tag.description: Optional tag the service instance must carry

passing.description: Set true to return only instances whose checks are all passing

tools.name: kv_get
tools.description: Read one entry from the Consul KV store by key. The value comes back base64-encoded, as Consul returns it

key.description: KV key path, without a leading slash (e.g. app/config)

dc.description: Optional datacenter to query instead of the agent's own

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, AND THE DOCS SAY THE SAME THING: Consul's HTTP API takes an ACL token in the X-Consul-Token request header (https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs, 'Authentication'), so {type: header, header: X-Consul-Token, template: '{{token}}'} is unchanged. The vault entry (integrationTypeRegistry.hashicorp_consul) sends the identical header in testHeaders and its testEndpoint is base_url + /v1/agent/self, which is this spec's test block verbatim. Consul also accepts the same token as a Bearer credential; the documented X-Consul-Token form is used because it is what the vault already proves against.

THE SCAFFOLD FLAGGED 'auth_field_optional_in_registry:token' AND IT IS ACCURATE: the registry marks token required:false because an agent with ACLs disabled answers every read here unauthenticated. This spec still lists token in requiredFields, because auth.template must reference a declared credential field and because any ACL-enabled instance (the only sane production posture) needs one. On an ACL-disabled instance the header is sent and ignored.

BASE URL IS CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED, SO NOTHING HERE IS PROVABLE BLIND: Consul is self-hosted, base_url comes from the credential ({fromCredential: 'base_url'}), and there is no vendor-run host to shape-prove against. This spec is NOT SHAPE_PROVEN by a blind 401 sweep; it is marked for the live harness, which stands up an ephemeral Consul container and drives every tool against it.

CATEGORY: the scaffold wrote 'uncategorized', which is not one of the twelve values in use across this spec directory (cloud_hosting, commerce_finance, communication, crm_sales, data_ai, developer, files_knowledge, hr_hiring, marketing_email, media, monitoring, project_management). Changed to 'cloud_hosting', where the other platform control planes already sit (terraform, cloudflare, digitalocean, okta). The vault entry says 'security', which is not a spec-directory value and would in any case undersell a service-discovery catalogue.

PROBES RESOLVE ON A FRESH INSTANCE, BY CONSTRUCTION: agent_self, list_services and list_nodes need no resource at all and carry an empty _probe. health_service probes service='consul', the service every Consul SERVER agent registers for itself, so it answers on an otherwise empty cluster; on a client-only agent that name is absent, which is a topology fact, not a spec defect. kv_get probes key='quoxproof-live', the exact key the live provisioner writes into the KV store.

TWO SHAPES ARE ASSERTED AND ONE IS DELIBERATELY NOT: /v1/catalog/nodes, /v1/health/service/{service} and /v1/kv/{key} all answer with a TOP-LEVEL ARRAY, hence the '[]' root pick on three tools; the field names are Consul's own (Node ID/Node/Address/Datacenter/Meta, the health triple Node/Service/Checks, and the KV entry Key/Value/Flags/Session/LockIndex/CreateIndex/ModifyIndex). /v1/catalog/services is the exception: it answers with a map keyed by SERVICE NAME whose values are tag arrays, so there is no static dotted source to pick and the tool is truncate-only, the same route 21 other tools in this directory take for dynamic payloads.

kv_get RETURNS WHATEVER THE CUSTOMER STORED, BASE64-ENCODED AS CONSUL RETURNS IT: Consul's KV store is commonly used for configuration rather than secrets, but nothing stops a customer putting a secret there, so treat the value as sensitive. It is a GET against the customer's own Consul with the customer's own ACL token, and no tool enumerates keys: reading requires the caller to already know the key (the recurse and keys query parameters that would list a subtree are not wired).

NO CLAMPS: none of these five endpoints takes a limit, page or per_page parameter. Consul's catalogue and health reads are unpaginated and bound instead by filter, tag, passing and dc, which are exposed as optional inputs. rateLimit {windowMs: 60000, max: 30} is the directory default and is the only throttle here.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT: all five tools are GETs. The same API exposes PUT on /v1/agent/service/register, /v1/agent/check/register, /v1/kv/{key}, /v1/session/create and the maintenance-mode endpoints, PUT/DELETE across /v1/acl/*, and DELETE on /v1/kv/{key} and /v1/agent/service/deregister. None is wired here. Nothing in this connector may be described as managing a Consul cluster or a service mesh.

NAMESPACE IS CLEAN FOR THIS ID: no static agent tool in lib/agentTools.js begins with 'hashicorp_consul_', and no other connector id prefixes or is prefixed by it (the sibling hashicorp_nomad is a distinct prefix, not an overlap). The routed names are hashicorp_consul_agent_self, hashicorp_consul_list_services, hashicorp_consul_list_nodes, hashicorp_consul_health_service and hashicorp_consul_kv_get, all within the 64-character routed-name limit.
